deployment: Catalogued as opt-in profile yidj2, ranked after yid and heb; not in the Tesseract image's models.lock, the BOINC worker or any route. Stock yid stays the default until the newspaper score decides (#1479 step 4).

caveats: test pages are unseen pages of the 60 books trained on, so the gain on other books is probably smaller
run 2, the dictionary comparison and the snapshot comparison were chosen after seeing run 1's result
no newspaper accuracy: that needs the transcribed set in ocr/bench/yiddish-newspaper
evaluation.format: lists are [estimate, lower 95% limit, upper 95% limit]; CER is mean page CER

newspaper_agreement_with_jochre3_percent.note: symmetric edit distance on 100 newspaper crops: agreement, not accuracy

evaluation.study: Study 10 (PR #1428), not preregistered; Study 8's references, scorer (YIVO-simplifies both sides) and page bootstrap
evaluation.test_set: the corpus's 104-page test split: whole pages at PSM 3, and its 4,011 ALTO line crops at PSM 7

model.dictionaries: word, punctuation and number dawgs rebuilt in visual order by tesstrain (LANG_TYPE=RTL) from the start model's own 20,582 words
model.kind: Tesseract 5 LSTM, float, written by lstmtraining --stop_training
model.name: yidj2

recipe.steps: study10.sh --work DIR --step image, setup, lines, langdata, train, then --step snap --run yidj2 --name yidj2 --checkpoint yidj2_1.470_16289_52300.checkpoint

reproducibility.conversion: yidj2.traineddata was converted from the run's checkpoint through study10.sh --step snap
reproducibility.recipe_checked: study10.sh, run as the recipe, rebuilt the stock-network yidrev model and run 1's 17,900-iteration model byte for byte, selected the same 20,509 lines for run 2 and fetched the same langdata
reproducibility.training_repeated: yes: run 2 was repeated on CT 240 on 2026-11-05 (#1479) from the same lines and tools, with the unicharset order below and OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2 where Study 10 used one thread. All 600 progress lines and the checkpoint names matched Study 10's, and the 52,300-iteration checkpoint converted to a yidj2.traineddata identical byte for byte
reproducibility.unicharset_order: tesstrain concatenates all-gt in find order over the line folder, and the 29 characters not in stock yid enter the unicharset in first-seen order, so a fresh copy of the same lines gave the same 102 characters in another order and a different network. Putting those characters first in all-gt, in the order of entries 73-101 of yidj2.traineddata's lstm-unicharset, rebuilt Study 10's unicharset and proto model byte for byte (#1479)

tools.tesseract: 5.5.0 (Debian 5.5.0-1+b1), the usnm_ocr Tesseract image built from ocr/engines/tesseract at cf07f950
tools.trainer_image: that image plus make, python3, python3-pil, python3-bidi and wget (recipe tesstrain.Containerfile)

training.duration: 1 h 24 min on one CPU thread at nice 19
training.stopped: 60,000 iterations; the model is the newest best checkpoint (52,300), chosen on training error, not test score

training_data.attribution: Assaf Urieli and the Yiddish Book Center
training_data.citation: Assaf Urieli, Amber Clooney, Michelle Sigiel and Grisha Leyfer, "Jochre 3 and the Yiddish OCR corpus", 2025, arXiv:2501.08442
training_data.held_out: the 104-page test split; it shares all 60 books with the training split, and no page is in both

page_list.columns: image sha256, ALTO sha256, image path

training_data.text: each ALTO text line in NFC, logical order, cut with its line image (cut-lines.py)
